title: Quantum Stochastic Inflation
summary: This paper derives stochastic inflation as the reduced dynamics of a coarse-grained quantum field treated as an open quantum system. The coarse-grained field and total patch momentum form a canonical pair, and tracing over the decoupled boundary mode yields a one-channel GKLS equation. Its Wigner-Weyl transform reproduces the stochastic-inflation Fokker-Planck equation.
main_results: The canonical coarse-grained field and total patch momentum form the correct retained bulk variables.
The moving coarse-graining boundary induces a single non-Hermitian Lindblad channel.
Hubble friction and stochastic diffusion arise from the same completely positive boundary map.
The Wigner-Weyl transform of the GKLS equation reproduces the stochastic-inflation phase-space Fokker-Planck equation.
The light-field overdamped limit recovers the slow-roll Starobinsky stochastic equation.
Heavy fields remain closer to pure underdamped quantum oscillators and do not admit the same classical stochastic limit.

arxiv.comments: 51 pages, 3 figures. Source files and supporting code are available in the GitHub repository.
